body:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by an independent reviewer on T158's diff. Out of T158's scope: T158 is about the render CLOCKS, and this is the read path.

WHAT IS WRONG. `paint` stamps every render with an EPOCH, so a render the world moved past paints nothing. The gesture path has no such stamp. `gesture`'s resolve and reject callbacks close over the VARIABLE `reads`, and `darken` drops the maps by REASSIGNING `reads = {}` and `state = {}`. So a `loam_query` issued before a teardown writes its PRE-teardown answer into the FRESH map. Nothing paints at once, because `root` is null. The entry survives, and the next successful `foldRoot` paints with it.

THE SAME HOLE IS ON THE ERASURE PATH. `foldRoot`'s `rootMoved` branch clears `reads` and bumps the epoch, but it cannot cancel an outstanding gesture. A pre-erasure drill-down therefore lands in the post-erasure map. The shell's own header calls the dropped maps a completeness claim — 'no pre-erasure answer can be replayed from the viewer's side of the wall'. That claim is currently false for one call in flight, which is the H7 family: a report that can be false.

A SECOND, SMALLER FACE. The reject branch overwrites `line.textContent`, so a stale gesture error replaces `darken`'s connector guidance. The viewer is told to fix the wrong thing.

THE REPAIR is the discipline the render path already has: stamp each gesture with the epoch it was issued under, and DROP the answer when it is stale rather than folding it in. Nothing else in the shell needs to change.

RAILS: two-sided at both levels. At the BEHAVIOUR level, drive the emitted shell — a gesture in flight, then a darkening event, then a later data event; assert the pre-teardown reading is absent from what the bundle receives, AND assert that a gesture answered with no teardown in between IS folded in. At the BYTES level, assert the emitted page carries the epoch stamp on the gesture path. A rail that only proves the drop cannot see an over-eager one, which would silently break every drill-down.

ADDED 2026-08-12 (main thread, folding in a duplicate shard I opened in error before this one had landed):

MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING, the discipline T158 itself followed. Drive the real page, put a mediated read in flight, tear down — and separately, ERASE — underneath it, and record whether the stale answer lands. A finding that cannot be reproduced is a hypothesis; say so and close this ticket if that is what the evidence shows.

AND PREFER THE EXISTING EPOCH to a second notion of currency. Two clocks that must agree is precisely the defect T139 and T158 both turned out to be; do not repair one instance of that shape by minting another.

WHO MERGES: if the fix only DISCARDS a stale answer, it makes a report more honest and self-merges on the ordinary bar. If it changes what any reader can observe across an ERASURE, that is Myk's — say which in one line in the PR.
title: A mediated read in flight survives a teardown — the page's gesture path has no epoch
